event: Daily Intelligence Briefing
title: Daily Market Briefing
text:
BOTTOM LINE — Semis-led rout, defensive bid, no panic capitulation.
Oct PPI (released 11/13) printed 0.3% m/m vs 0.4% fc and 6.5% y/y vs 6.6% fc, yet the tape sold the growth/AI complex hard — SOXX -5.41%, QQQ -2.67%, with money rotating into XLP +0.27% and XLU +0.18%. A soft inflation print that buys no relief rally tells you positioning, not macro, drove today: semis were crowded, and the exit was orderly (SPY 1.5x volume on a down day = distribution, but breadth at 48 new 60d highs vs 23 lows shows no washout).

INDICES — VIX 22.9, +9.03% on VIXY, above its 19.6 20-day MA.
RSP -1.01%, DIA -1.43%, IWM -1.66%, SPY -1.91%, QQQ -2.67%, SOXX -5.41%. Small beat large by 0.69pp. QQQ is below its 200-day MA — that is the CTA sell trigger live. Bonds bid (IEF +0.22%), dollar firm (UUP +0.20%), oil -3.81% (USO), silver -3.94%.

VOLUME & BREADTH — SPY 1.5x and SOXX 1.5x on down days: distribution in the index and in semis; QQQ 0.9x means the megacap unwind came on light volume — low-conviction selling inside a high-conviction semi exit. RSP 1.0x and IJH 0.9x: rotation out of small/mid was ignored, i.e. nobody dumped the broad market. Breadth: 65% above 50DMA, 59% above 200DMA, adv/dec 145/355, up/down volume 0.26, 48 highs vs 23 lows — participation is deteriorating but not breaking; this was a narrow leadership hit, not a broad tape failure.

SECTORS & ROTATION — XLP Staples +0.27%, XLU Utilities +0.18%, XLRE Real Estate -0.27%, XLV Healthcare -0.51%, XLF Financials -0.85%, XLB Materials -1.46%, XLY Discretionary -1.53%, XLC Comms -1.72%, XLI Industrials -1.85%, XLE Energy -1.96%, XLK Technology -3.24%.
Top industries: JETS +0.62%, KIE +0.61%; bottom: DRAM -7.38%, WGMI -6.82%, SOXX -5.41%.
Flows confirm the memory unwind but not the price ranking: SOXX +$24,659mm (100p), QQQ +$14,374mm (100p) inflows against XLK's -3.24% — buyers are adding into the drawdown while XLU -$510mm (4p) and XLE -$455mm (15p) bleed despite outperforming.
Money-in: defensives (XLP, XLU) and semi ETFs on the dip; money-out: energy, financials, utilities flow-wise. Label: defensive risk-off.

POSITIONING — SPY PCR 1.60 and IWM PCR 2.85 = heavy protection demand; skews positive (SPY +13.4%, QQQ +10.4%) confirm put premium. QQQ ATM IV 40.2% vs VIX 22.9 and VIXEQ 46.5 vs VIX 22.9 — a 23.6-point constituent-over-index gap = high dispersion, low implied correlation, stock-picker's tape. VVIX 114.2 above its 103.7 MA; MOVE data unavailable, so no bond-vol read.

CROSS-ASSET — Silver -3.94% (SLV) with gold -0.71% and oil -3.81%: a growth-scare deflation impulse dragging commodities while Treasuries catch a safe-haven bid (IEF +0.22%) — equities selling without a rate spike is the tell that this is an AI/semis de-risking, not a macro repricing. Next FOMC: Dec 9, 2026; CME FedWatch shows hike 100%, hold 0%, cut 0%. Polymarket: 5% for a 50bp+ hike (5d -6pp), 92% that the upper bound reaches 4.25% before 2027.

SIGNALS & WATCH — Fear & Greed 59.4, Neutral.
MU -7.62%, MRVL -7.27%, TER -7.07% — MU/MRVL traded on the semis tape, not a company result; TER's headline is a Jefferies bullish initiation, so its -7.07% is pure sector beta. Vol spikes: GS 2.3x with -2.73% = distribution in the banks; SILJ 2.1x with -4.85% = distribution in silver miners. Momentum extremes: XLK -11.40% is the worst 20d sector; QUAL BEAR z-score -1.73 over 259 days is the extreme regime read. Watch: SOXX -5.41% (below-cost dip buying at 100p percentile flow into a 200d break), IWM -1.66% (PCR 2.85 puts, small-large spread only 0.69pp), SLV (ATM IV 53.0% with PCR 0.25 — lopsided call positioning into a -17.75% 20d slide).
